title: Spatially resolved electrical modelling of cracks and other inhomogeneities in crystalline silicon solar cells
mechanism: Quasi-SPICE network model of active and inactive microcracks built from EL damage maps; a cell region becomes inactive when cracks cut it off electrically from the busbars.
adaptation: Rule renderer for inactive: draw a crack curve on a train cell with crack but no inactive, compute regions isolated from every busbar along the finger direction, darken them by the source-specific inactive/active intensity ratio measured on the 42 train inactive cells (plus noise and edge blur), label inactive and crack. Gives pairs that respect 'inactive always touches a crack'. Also yields inactive-area fraction for severity bands.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + rule-rendered crack+inactive cells, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF 5 seeds. Metric: module-grouped 5-fold CV inactive IoU and BMRK inactive IoU. Kill: CV inactive IoU gain < +0.02.
evidence: R: model validated on experimental cells; 0.12% error in power-loss estimate for a complexly damaged cell. No ML or image-synthesis evidence.
prior_overlap: None; physics simulation of EL is listed as never tried.
